title: Cobalt flask and the shadow of its own knurl

tokens.v: Full-bleed photograph filling the entire frame edge to edge with no border, frame, letterbox band or matte of any kind. One bare fresnel head sits low and close at camera-left and the flask's own machining does the art direction: the knurled cap throws its teeth onto a raw lime-plaster wall behind as a two-metre sawtooth band, every tooth crisp and repeating, while the polished base band curves that same source back onto the plaster as a bright caustic arc above it and the body drops one long shadow out of the bottom-right corner. The matte cobalt coat refuses to shine, so cap and base band are the only specular in the frame and both fire hard. 85mm at f/11 from just below cap height, deep focus from flask to trowel marks, the flask left of centre at roughly sixty-five percent of the frame height. NORTHWARD is laser-etched through the coat to bare steel across the upper body in capitals large enough to read at a glance, taking exactly one highlight. Nothing sits between lens and flask: the near floor is swept empty and falls to black at the bottom edge.
